name: Toyota GR Corolla
torque: 273 lb-ft @ 3,000–5,500 rpm (295 lb-ft on the 2025 8-speed automatic)
drivetrain: AWD (GR-FOUR, with 60:40 / 50:50 / 30:70 selectable front-rear torque split)
transmission: 6-speed intelligent manual (iMT, with auto rev-match) · an 8-speed automatic (GR-DAT) was added for 2025
curb_weight: ~3,175–3,285 lbs (the stripped, rear-seat-delete Morizo Edition is the lightest)
reliability: 8/10 — the G16E-GTS is the most powerful production three-cylinder ever sold, and it has held up well: independent testing and KBB give it top marks, and there are no widespread catastrophic-failure patterns despite the huge specific output. The caveats are that it is a young, high-strung platform running a lot of boost through a small engine, and a few very public cases (including two engine fires) saw Toyota deny warranty claims — rare, but a reminder to buy one with a clean, documented history. Treat it as a hard-driven performance car, not a Corolla.
cost_to_own: Insurance: High (300 hp AWD performance car) · Maintenance ~$450–600/yr · Turbo-AWD running costs (tires, brakes, clutch on tracked cars) run higher than a normal Corolla · Strong demand keeps resale high
popular_mods: A tune / higher-octane calibration — the G16E responds well and there is real headroom on E85
An upgraded intercooler and intake to keep intake temps down on repeated hard runs
A cat-back or turbo-back exhaust for the three-cylinder's distinctive off-beat note
Sticky 200-treadwear tires and pads — the GR-FOUR chassis rewards grip and cooling more than power
Honest take: it is quick and capable stock; sort cooling, tires, and brakes before chasing more boost
oil_interval: Every 5,000 miles (or sooner with track use — this engine works hard)

generations.Core / Circuit / Morizo (2023): The launch cars. Core is the value pick; Circuit adds a forged carbon roof, vents, and a rear spoiler; the limited Morizo Edition deletes the rear seat, shortens the gearing, and adds chassis bracing for a lighter, sharper track weapon.
generations.2024–present: Largely carryover on the manual, with a Premium grade added and running refinements. For 2025 Toyota added the 8-speed GR-DAT automatic (with a small torque bump) and light suspension/cooling updates, broadening the car's appeal beyond three-pedal buyers.

common_issues: A young, high-output platform — long-term durability data is still thin compared with a mainstream Corolla
A few high-profile warranty disputes (including engine fires) where Toyota denied claims — uncommon, but check history
Real heat generation under sustained track use; intake temps and brake fade are the limits to manage
Firm, buzzy three-cylinder character and a busy ride — this is a rally-bred hatch, not a quiet commuter
High demand meant markups and limited allocation, especially on the Morizo Edition
maintenance_tips: Change the oil on a short interval with the specified 0W-20 synthetic, and shorter still if you track it
Let the turbo three warm up before boost and cool down after hard runs before shutting off
Watch intake and coolant temps on track; add cooling before adding power
Keep every service record — documented history matters a lot on a warranty-sensitive performance car
Inspect the clutch, brakes, and tires regularly on any car that has seen track or autocross use
